covers.quote: So, it’s important to ensure your narrative is based on evidence from authoritative sources or actual events.
Don’t include details that might work with the story but aren’t factual.
And never include any information based on an assumption that something happened because of something else.

rules.quote: Government content must be evidence-based and created transparently.
rules.violation_condition: content asserting facts or causal connections without supporting evidence, or containing non-factual details to suit a narrative
rules.why: G-2, G-4: The section establishes a strict requirement for evidence-based narrative in government content and specifies negative conditions (no non-factual story details, no unsupported assumptions of cause and effect).

rules.quote: Omit anything that isn’t related to your primary message.
rules.violation_condition: content included in the body/middle section that does not relate to the primary message
rules.why: Direct instruction on text composition restricting irrelevant content in the middle of a narrative.

rules.quote: There must be a logical connection between the 3 parts.
rules.violation_condition: a narrative lacking logical connection or continuity between the beginning, middle, and end
rules.why: Clear structural constraint on multi-part narrative writing.
